gen-dafont-quantum-gf-krub: Krub reads tall and contemporary, curves stopping just short of closing. Quantum is at its best as stencil-cut letters of one steady width, while Krub earns its place with open loops and a pronounced x-height.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-lexend: Clean, techy and loosely spaced up top, with an oversized lowercase underneath. And Quantum is best at compressed ascenders and loose letterfit, while the plain sans Lexend is best at open curves.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-mada: Crisp techy lettering over a towering midzone whose curves refuse to close. But what stands out most is how Quantum's strokes keep identical weight while Mada stays open and tall.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-nokora: Crisp tech lettering over a dense, dark body. What lingers is how Quantum's pen never shifts pressure or angle, while Nokora lays down a thick, dark lowercase stripe with a wide-open s.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-chakma: Quantum draws every letter with uninterrupted line width, set against Noto Sans Chakma, whose lowercase packs up toward the caps. Quantum earns its keep when it's big and brief.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Noto Sans Ethiopic reads sturdy and modern, its tall lowercase carrying c terminals that hang far from the bowl. Under Quantum's swell-free bowls, the text should move along steadily.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-georgian: Noto Sans Georgian reads open and modern, with short ascender stems. What holds the pair together is Quantum's steady line, free of any pressure variation, against Georgian's generous curve apertures.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Noto Sans Gothic gives the sans lowercase counters like drilled glass beads. Quantum does its best work with flat, brush-free strokes and loose letterfit, while the Gothic forms curve like open parentheses.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Noto Sans Grantha reads smooth, tall little letters like flattened nib bowls. Across a whole stretch of text the eye never snags on a closed-up bowl, a quiet follow-up to Quantum's marker-traced letters.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Noto Sans Hebrew fills its line with a dominant midsection. Wide gaps between curve ends and stems keep the text breathing across long lines, while Quantum's rounds and stems share one weight.
